translations.text: Aleph. How the city that was full of people sits alone! She has become a widow, she who ruled over nations. She who ruled over provinces has been subjected to forced labor.
Waw. They stripped the daughter of Zion of all her splendor. Her princes became like rams that found no pasture, and they went weakly before those who pursued them.

Zayin. In the days of her humiliation, Jerusalem remembered all her former delights, when her people were [?] into the hands of their enemies and there was no one to help her. Her enemies saw her when she went into exile and laughed at her.
Heth. Jerusalem sinned grievously, and because of this she was shaken. All who praised her dishonored her, because they saw her shame when she lamented and fell backward.
Mem. From on high he sent fire and scorched my bones. He spread his net for my feet and turned me backward. He laid me waste and made me suffer all day long.
Qoph. I called my friends, but they turned a deaf ear to me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while they searched for food to restore their lives and found none.
Shin. Hear how I groan, with no one to comfort me. All my enemies heard of my suffering and rejoiced because you had done it. You brought the day you proclaimed, and they became like me.
He. The Lord became like an enemy to me and swallowed up Israel. He swallowed up all her glory and laid waste her strongholds. He increased the humiliation of the disgraced daughter of Judah.
Teth. Her gates sank into the ground. Her bars were cast aside and shattered. Her king and her princes are among the nations; she has no law. Her prophets saw no vision from the Lord.

Yod. The elders of the daughter of Zion sat on the ground in silence. They put dust on their heads and wrapped themselves in sackcloth. They brought the princes and the young women of Jerusalem down to the ground.

Samekh. All who passed along the road clapped their hands at you. They hissed and shook their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, “Is this the city that is the crown, the glory, and the joy of the whole earth?”

Resh. Look, Lord, and see whom you have stripped bare like this. Should women eat the fruit of their wombs, the infants they nurse? Or should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
Gimel. I cry out and wail, because my prayer has been brought to an end.
My soul has given up hope of peace, and I have forgotten what is good.
For the Lord will not abandon them forever.
To deprive a person of justice in the presence of the Most High.
A river of water flows from our eyes because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.
Shin. You heard all their insults, Lord, and all their schemes against me.
Repay them and take vengeance on them according to the work of their hands.
Waw. The sin of the daughter of my people was greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant, without hands laboring over her.
Teth. Those killed in battle were better off than those killed by hunger. They passed away, pierced through at the Lord’s command.
Our inheritance has gone to strangers, and my houses to foreigners.
The joy of our hearts has ceased; our song has turned into mourning.
Because of this our hearts grew sick; because of these things our eyes grew dark.
Because Mount Zion has become a wilderness, foxes roam over it.
